bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar govt hikes DA, DR for employees and pensioners ahead of Chhath festival
bihar_raw_news.content: Policy 3 min Read Bihar govt hikes DA, DR for employees and pensioners ahead of Chhath festival The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. It has come as a great relief for state government employees and pensioners ahead of Chhath Puja. PTI Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 09:33 PM IST Set ETGovernment as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment For employees and pensioners under the 5th Pay Commission structure, the DA/DR rate has been enhanced from 483 per cent to 497 per cent. Bihar Cabinet on Tuesday approved an increase in the dearness allowance for its employees and dearness relief for pensioners with effect from July 1, 2026. The decision was taken at a Cabinet meeting chaired by Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary. It has come as a great relief for state government employees and pensioners ahead of Chhath Puja. According to the Finance Department proposal approved by the Cabinet, "Under the 7th Pay Commission structure, DA/DR has been raised from 60 per cent to 63 per cent, while those covered by the 6th Pay Commission will receive an increase from 262 per cent to 269 per cent." For employees and pensioners under the 5th Pay Commission structure, the DA/DR rate has been enhanced from 483 per cent to 497 per cent. The revised rates will benefit serving state government employees, pensioners and family pensioners covered under the respective pay structures, said a senior official of the finance department. The Cabinet also approved the implementation of the Modified Assured Career Progression Scheme for regular employees of urban local bodies in the state. "The decision is aimed at providing financial advancement to employees who often retire after serving for years in the same post without any promotion or career progression opportunities. "The move follows long-standing demands from urban local body employees, who lacked provisions for regular promotions", said the approved proposal of the Urban Development and Housing Department, The government is of the view that the scheme would boost employees' motivation, efficiency and commitment towards discharging their duties and responsibilities, said an official. To encourage innovation, entrepreneurship and startup culture among female students studying in higher educational institutions, and to develop their innovative ideas into practical business ventures, the Cabinet approved the launch of the " Bihar Ki Beti Startup Challenge Scheme " (Bihar's Daughter Startup Challenge Scheme). "The scheme will benefit a maximum of 2,100 female students, starting from the current financial year. It will remain in operation for four financial years, from 2026-27 to 2029-30. Administrative approval of ₹88.20 crore has been granted for the implementation of the scheme", said the approved proposal of the Higher Education Department. In an attempt to encourage the participation of female students in higher education and research, the Cabinet approved the launch of the " Mukhyamantri Balika PhD Fellowship Scheme ". bihar_raw_news.title: Patna Municipal Bonds List on NSE, Opening New Urban Funding Route
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Patna Municipal Bonds List on NSE, Opening New Urban Funding Route Breaking News Patna Municipal Bonds List on NSE, Opening New Urban Funding Route By Ananya Sharma November 11, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp Patna Municipal Corporation’s Rs 200-crore municipal bonds were listed on the National Stock Exchange on Tuesday, creating a new funding route for Bihar’s civic infrastructure and prompting the state government to ask other urban local bodies to explore market-based finance. Chief minister Samrat Choudhary rang the ceremonial bell at the listing event organised by Bihar’s urban development and housing department. Representatives of the NSE, including Krishna Iyyer, head of issuer relationships, product and business development, attended the ceremony in Patna. Deputy chief ministers Vijay Kumar Choudhary and Bijendra Prasad Yadav, urban development and housing minister Nitish Mishra, Patna mayor Sita Sahu and chief secretary Pratyaya Amrit were also present, according to the report. The listing marks the first time a municipal bond issued by a civic body in Bihar has been listed on the NSE. Choudhary described the Rs 200-crore issue as a significant achievement and urged other municipal corporations to consider similar funding options. He also called on urban local bodies to increase their own revenue and reduce their dependence on government funding. The chief minister said funds raised through municipal bonds and public-private partnership projects should be directed towards revenue-generating ventures so that they can continue to generate returns after loan repayments. The remarks place the bond issue within a wider push to strengthen the financial capacity of city administrations and link infrastructure spending with recurring revenue. Choudhary also proposed expanding Patna’s Marine Drive from its existing 26-km length to 126 km through a proposed investment of Rs 30,000 crore under the PPP model. He said the existing stretch had taken 13 years to complete using government funds, prompting the state to examine private participation for the proposed expansion. The address also covered energy, flood management, healthcare and planned urban growth. The chief minister said battery storage systems would be important to reduce the burden of purchasing electricity at varying rates. He said proposed memorandums of understanding during Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s expected November 21 visit to Bihar could include battery and pumped storage projects, with potential investments running into lakhs of crores of rupees. He urged financially well-off households to give up the benefit of 125 units of free electricity and install rooftop solar systems. Under the state’s support programme, households can receive around Rs 98,000 for a 3-kW solar system, while surplus electricity generated by them would be purchased by the government. For flood management and construction, Choudhary proposed extracting river silt both to generate revenue and to help control flooding, with the material being used in infrastructure projects. He also said the government would examine a brownfield PPP model under which experienced medical professionals could operate newly built medical colleges and hospitals. The state further highlighted plans for 12 greenfield satellite townships, including Pataliputra Township

bihar_raw_news.content: Urban Transportation 1 min Read Bihar CM launches water metro service on Ganga river in Patna "The service is also expected to provide commuters with an alternate route to the congested Ashok Rajpath," an official said. PTI Published On Nov 10, 2026 at 08:48 PM IST Set ETInfra as your preferred source on Google Share Icon Copy Link Share on Whatsapp Share on Linkedin Share on X Share on Telegram Share on Facebook Bookmark Comment The fare is ₹50 for each adult. Bihar Chief Minister Samrat Choudhary on Tuesday launched a catamaran service on the Ganga river between Digha Ghat and Gandhi Ghat in Patna , aiming to promote eco-friendly tourism and provide an alternative mode of transport. Flagging off the water metro service from Digha Ghat, the chief minister said the state tourism department's initiative would offer tourists and locals a modern and convenient transport facility while boosting river tourism . "The service is also expected to provide commuters with an alternate route to the congested Ashok Rajpath," an official said. The 50-seater vessel is equipped with a hybrid engine , primarily operating on electric power, helping minimise air, water and noise pollution, said a statement issued by the Chief Minister's Office. It has facilities such as air-conditioning, a public announcement system, toilets and wheelchair accessibility. The service will operate between Digha and Gandhi Ghat, with plans to extend it to Kangan Ghat in the future. Fast and shore charging facilities have been installed at Digha and Gandhi Ghats. The fare is ₹50 for each adult. Children below five years can travel free, while those aged between five and 12 will be charged half the adult fare, the statement said. Tickets are currently available at the counter at Digha Ghat, with online booking expected to be introduced soon. Comments What are your thoughts?

bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar Building Bylaws 2026 Bring 30-Day Deemed Approval - Urban Acres
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar Building Bylaws 2026 Bring 30-Day Deemed Approval Breaking News Bihar Building Bylaws 2026 Bring 30-Day Deemed Approval By Ananya Sharma November 11, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Bihar cabinet has approved the Building Bylaws 2026, introducing deemed approval of building maps if local urban bodies do not clear applications within 30 days and replacing the rules framed in 2014. The new regulations were approved on Tuesday following a proposal from the urban development and housing department, Cabinet secretariat additional chief secretary Arwind Kumar Choudhary said, according to a report by the Times of India. The rules classify residential and commercial buildings according to risk, introduce restrictions through a negative list for builders and set out provisions linked to floor area ratio (FAR). Buildings up to 10 metres in height have been classified as low risk, those between 10 metres and 24 metres as medium risk, and structures above 24 metres as high risk. The classification is intended to establish different regulatory requirements based on the scale and potential risks associated with a building. The bylaws allow an approach road of up to 3.7 metres and require a setback on only one side in specified circumstances, enabling emergency vehicles to access a building from the rear. Parking space will be calculated at 15 square metres per vehicle. The rules also allow building map approvals to be revalidated for five years, with automatic revalidation on payment of the prescribed fee. Owners of existing buildings will be able to obtain permits by paying the prescribed fee and submitting building maps. The cabinet decision also incorporates fire safety provisions into the building permit process, making fire-related compliance part of the approval framework. The regulations offer additional development potential for buildings that secure green-building certification. Buildings with three-star certification will be eligible for an additional 5% FAR, while four-star and five-star buildings will receive 10% and 15% additional FAR, respectively. FAR determines the total floor area that can be constructed on a plot relative to its size. The deemed approval provision could reduce delays for applicants where local urban bodies do not decide applications within the 30-day period. Its operation will depend on how applications are received, scrutinised and recorded, and on the procedures that urban bodies adopt for enforcing the new rules. The cabinet announcement, as reported, did not specify how disputes or incomplete applications will be handled under the deemed-clearance mechanism. The cabinet also approved decisions outside the building regulations. Dearness allowance for government employees, pensioners and family pensioners covered by the fifth, sixth and seventh pay commissions was increased retrospectively from July 1. The revisions raise the rates from 483% to 497% for the fifth pay commission, from 262% to 269% for the sixth and from 60% to 63% for the seventh. The changes will impose an additional annual burden of Rs 1,088 crore on the state exchequer. In another decision, the cabinet approved the Bihar Artificial Intelligence Mission. bihar_raw_news.title: Bihar IAS Promotions Lift Key Urban Officials to Higher Ranks
bihar_raw_news.content: Home Breaking News Bihar IAS Promotions Lift Key Urban Officials to Higher Ranks Breaking News Bihar IAS Promotions Lift Key Urban Officials to Higher Ranks By Ananya Sharma November 11, 2026 0 Copy URL Facebook Linkedin X WhatsApp The Bihar government promoted 30 IAS officers on Tuesday, elevating two senior officials to additional chief secretary rank and placing officers associated with road construction, disaster management, district administration and the Patna Municipal Corporation in higher grades. Santosh Kumar Mall, principal secretary in the disaster management department, and Pankaj Kumar, principal secretary in the home department, were promoted to the rank of additional chief secretary, according to the report. The elevation comes as Bihar’s administrative structure continues to manage responsibilities spanning public safety, civic services and infrastructure delivery. Road construction department secretary Pankaj Kumar Pal was placed in the rank of principal secretary. The department is responsible for a major part of the state’s road infrastructure administration, although the report did not specify any change in his posting or announce any new project linked to the promotion. The government also promoted several officers to secretary rank. They include Himanshu Kumar Sharma, special secretary in the science, technology and technical education department; Shirsat Kapil Ashok, managing director of Comfed; Nilesh Ramchandra Deore; Ujjwal Kumar, special secretary in the rural development department; Naresh Jha, settlement officer in Katihar; Brajesh Kumar, settlement officer in Madhepura; Navin Kumar, special secretary in the prohibition, excise and registration department; and Udyan Mishra, special secretary in the tourism department. The list also includes officers whose work is directly connected with district-level administration and urban service delivery. Nalanda district magistrate Udita Singh, Samastipur district magistrate Roshan Kushwaha and Gaya district magistrate Shashank Shubhankar were elevated to the rank of special secretary. District magistrates oversee coordination between state departments and local administrations, but the report did not indicate whether the officers would retain their current postings. Panchayati raj additional secretary Aditya Prakash and revenue and land reforms additional secretary Amit Kumar Pandey were also promoted to special secretary rank. Their departments deal with local government administration and land-related processes, both of which affect how public infrastructure, development activity and civic expansion are administered across Bihar. Yashpal Meena, commissioner of the Patna Municipal Corporation, was among the officers elevated to special secretary rank. The promotion affects his administrative rank; the supplied report does not state that he has been transferred or that the corporation’s responsibilities have changed. The municipal commissioner’s position is responsible for the functioning of Patna’s civic administration, including the implementation of municipal services within the city. The promotions therefore span state departments, district administrations and a major municipal body. The order, as reported, changes the officers’ ranks but does not provide details on revised postings, additional responsibilities, implementation dates or any departmental reshuffle that may follow. Further administrative orders would be required to establish whether the promotions lead to changes in assignments. national_raw_news.title: Govt invites fresh applications under PLI scheme for medical devices
national_raw_news.content: The Government has invited fresh applications under the Production Linked Incentive Scheme for Promoting Domestic Manufacturing of Medical Devices (PLI-MD), which has now been extended up to the year 2035-36. An outlay of approximately two thousand 700 crore rupees available under the scheme will be utilized for the purpose. The applicants can submit applications through an online portal, which will be operational in the next 10 days. The Ministry of Chemicals and Fertilizers said that on the basis of learnings in the first phase of the Scheme, a number of simplifications have been done in the eligibility conditions as well as procedure for claiming incentive by the applicants. The applicants shall be allowed three years for setting up their manufacturing facilities in any of the four Target Segments (TS) which are medical consumables, disposables and implants, Critical components, high-end medical devices which are presently at a nascent stage of domestic manufacturing and high-end medical devices that are presently only assembled in the country. Under the PLI-MD 2.0, the minimum sales threshold requirement to claim incentive has been discontinued and minimum investment requirement has also been trimmed. To enhance ease of doing business, the scheme guidelines have been made easier and investor friendly. The applicants shall be free to submit any number of applications in one or more TS and the application window shall remain continuously open over a long period of time.
